text: As they approached Jerusalem, coming to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples ahead,
telling them, "Go into the village ahead of you. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord needs it, and he will send it back here shortly.'"
They went and found a colt tied at a doorway out in the street, and they untied it.
Some of the people standing there asked them, "What are you doing, untying that colt?"
They answered as Jesus had told them, and the people let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and he sat on it.
Many people spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut in the fields.
Those who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"
Then he entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything, and since it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, he went to find out whether it had any fruit. But when he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
So he said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again." And his disciples heard him.

They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus went into the temple and began driving out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves,
and he would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple.
And he taught them, saying, "Is it not written: 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it a den of robbers."
The chief priests and the scribes heard this and began looking for a way to destroy him, for they were afraid of him, since the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.

versions.text: The chief priests and the scribes heard this and began looking for a way to destroy him, for they were afraid of him, since the whole crowd was captivated by his teaching.
versions.explanation: ἐξεπλήσσετο means "was astonished/amazed," conveying overwhelming wonder; "captivated" softens the sense of astonishment.

text: And when evening came, they went out of the city.
In the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
Peter remembered and said to him, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered."
Jesus answered them, "Have faith in God.
Truly I tell you, if anyone says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will be done for him.
Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive whatever you hold against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.

versions.text: And whenever you stand praying, forgive whatever you hold against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses."
versions.explanation: The closing quotation mark here ends Jesus' speech prematurely, leaving verse 26 (which continues his words) outside the quotation. Remove the closing mark here and close the quotation at the end of verse 26.

text: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses." [footnote: Some early manuscripts do not contain this verse.]

versions.text: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses.
versions.explanation: This verse is absent from many early manuscripts; a brief footnote is helpful for readers, and the quotation should be closed here since Jesus' words continue from verse 25.

text: They came again to Jerusalem, and as Jesus was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him.
"By what authority are you doing these things?" they asked. "And who gave you the authority to do this?"
Jesus replied, "I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
John's baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer me."
They discussed it among themselves, saying, "What shall we say? If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'

versions.text: They discussed it among themselves: "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will ask, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
versions.explanation: The clause Τί εἴπωμεν; ("What shall we say?") is omitted from the translation. It is part of the Greek text and adds to the deliberation's dramatic rhythm.

text: But if we say, 'From men'—" They were afraid of the crowd, for everyone held that John really was a prophet.
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." And Jesus said to them, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
